articles.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
articles.summary: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle. ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club.
body: Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. “My way, my idea, is that the best way to defend is to have the ball”. The problem with that is that only the three promoted sides have had less possession than Palace. “Here every mistake, every situation that is bad for the team will be a goal,” Sage added.

Palace conceded two goal against Beşiktaş on Thursday to the only shots on target they conceded. Newcastle similarly scored with both their shots on target. “We conceded fewer chances with our defending in open play today but it’s not enough,” the Palace manager said. “For the moment the pressure is always the same because I don’t find the solution. Today was not a tactical problem but a mental problem. When we came back from the dressing room we let our opponents have too many things. When you don’t control the ball you give the initiative to the opposition.”

articles.title: Chaos or concern - Hanley's striker cameo poses questions for Hibs
articles.summary: Grant Hanley was called upon to be a makeshift striker for Hibs against Celtic, but what does it signal for the Scottish Premiership's bottom side?
body: With eight minutes to go at Easter Road on Sunday, Hibs needed a goal to salvage something from their Scottish Premiership match against Celtic.
Head coach Marink Reedijk turned to his bench in search of a spark and summoned old head Grant Hanley, tasking the grizzled centre-back with playing up front.
It was a damning indictment of the options available to Reedijk and also a sign of slight desperation after two defeats in his opening two matches in charge.
Hanley did have something of an impact during his short cameo. He won one header which led to a chance for Josh Mulligan and was close to getting on the end of a deflected effort from Rabbi Matondo.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
articles.summary: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone. Braga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at Motherwell. Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.
body: After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.
It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

articles.title: Rodgers lift Steelers past Saints in first NFL game in Paris
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers overtook Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history as the Pittsburgh Steelers beat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the first regular-season game to be played in Paris, France.
body: The four-time MVP quarterback surpassed Manning's tally of 539 touchdown passes with a first-half strike to tight end Darnell Washington and finished the game 19 of 30 for 212 yards as Mike McCarthy's Steelers improved to 5-2 on the year.

Saints quarterback Tyler Shough went 30 of 38 for 278 yards, a touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele and a second-half interception as Kellen Moore's side, honouring their deep-rooted French ties this week, dropped to 2-5.

Pittsburgh's Terrible Towels flew proudly while travelling Saints translated NOLA noise to Europe as the Stade de France welcomed 78,488 fans for the sixth of nine international games this season, Paris one of three first-time hosts for 2026 alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro.

Civil unrest in France had dominated build-up to Sunday's game after what began as peaceful demonstrations had turned into violence and looting, resulting in the cancellation of fan events and prompting an increased security presence across the city.

articles.title: Jarman claims historic second silver at Worlds
articles.summary: Jake Jarman becomes the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals at the same World Gymnastics Championships as he claims silver in the vault final.
body: Jake Jarman became the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals in the same World Gymnastics Championships as he claimed silver in the vault final.
Jarman had won silver in the men's floor on Saturday in Rotterdam to become Britain's most decorated athlete in the history of the event.
He achieved a score of 14.650 in the vault final as he finished second behind Armenia's Artur Davtyan, who took gold with 14.850.
"I'm just really happy. The aim is to land on my feet. I know that sounds simple but it really isn't," said 24-year-old Jarman, who has five World Championship medals overall in his career.

articles.title: Defender turns striker and scores in Bayern win
articles.summary: Bayern Munich beat Freiburg 3-1 away from home to reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga on Sunday (25). Dayot Upamecano was one of the standout performers, scoring the opener with a move in which he played the role of a pacey striker.
body: The defender won the ball inside Freiburg's own penalty area, played it sideways and kept running forward to lead the counterattack.
Michael Olise picked out Upamecano with an excellent through ball, and he showed composure to finish past the onrushing goalkeeper.
Freiburg spent almost the entire match struggling to threaten the opposition goal.
Late on, Tom Bischof scored an own goal, giving the home side fresh hope as they pushed for an equalizer and even forced a superb save from Jonas Urbig.

articles.title: Neville fears Carrick set to be sacked as Carra calls for decision tonight
articles.summary: Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher.
body: The humbling defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.
"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary.
On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him."
Carrick struck a defiant tone after the game but his lengthy applause towards the United fans after the final whistle was immediately interpreted as a farewell gesture.

articles.title: Kirk Herbstreit Goes Nuclear on Arch Manning’s Throw in Brutal On-Air Rant
articles.summary: Arch Manning is an emerging quarterback, and one of the most talented players right now in college football. Playing for the Texas Longhorns football program, he has a bright future ahead of him. Being a part of the prestigious Manning football family has made expectations on him high.
body: Manning played an important role as the Longhorns beat No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on October 24, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial. The team won with a score of 34-27. The quarterback completed 18 passes for 212 yards with one passing touchdown and two interceptions, and also added two rushing scores. Texas had built a 24-3 halftime advantage before Ole Miss mounted a comeback, though they still managed to secure the win.

During the fourth quarter of Texas’ victory, ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit sharply criticized Manning’s decision-making on a critical play. With the score tied at 24-24 and the Longhorns near their own 35-yard line on first down, Manning faced no immediate pressure. Despite that, he lofted a deep pass downfield into coverage featuring two defenders. The ball hung in the air long enough, and Ole Miss defensive back Jalyn Crawford intercepted the throw.
